cluster_protocol_history.2: openraft 0.10 — snapshot at POST /raft/snapshot, whole-snapshot (vote, meta, Vec<u8>); leader handoff at /raft/transfer-leader-msg. Bumped by commit 4a10c3d (2026-07-17). vote + append-entries stayed wire-compatible across this bump (measured, R625-S1); the snapshot path did not.
cluster_protocol_history.3: R706 (W294) — cluster secrets carry an ACCESS RULE. YubabaRequest::PutSecret and SecretRecord each gained `access: SecretAccess` (#[serde(default)] = deny-all). Nothing fails to PARSE in either direction, which is exactly why this needed a bump rather than a re-record: a mixed cluster is silently mis-authorized, not visibly broken. An epoch-2 node replicating an epoch-3 PutSecret drops the unknown `access` field on the floor and, having no check of its own, keeps serving that secret to ANY workload that names it — so the authorization guarantee R706 exists to create does not hold cluster-wide until every node is on 3. (The reverse direction is safe: an epoch-3 node applying an epoch-2 PutSecret defaults to deny-all and refuses, which is loud and re-fixable with `yah cloud secret put`.) Cheap moment to take: the fleet had zero cluster secrets and no node had a cluster KEK when this landed. CLUSTER_PROTOCOL is advertised on GET /health and in the signed release manifest — it is not a hard join gate — so this does not mechanically block a rolling upgrade; it makes the mixed window visible to the operator, which is the whole point here.
cluster_protocol_history.4: R732-F1 (W245) — tenant fencing epochs. `YubabaRequest` gained three variants (ClaimTenant, TransferTenant, RenewTenantLease), `YubabaResponse` gained `Tenant(TenantOutcome)`, and `YubabaState` gained `tenants: BTreeMap<TenantId, TenantOwnership>` (#[serde(default)]). The discriminator against BOTH prior precedents in this file: R706's `access` and R720-F1's `digest` added struct FIELDS, which serde tolerates in both directions (no deny_unknown_fields anywhere in this chain) — R706 was bumped only because a tolerated field made a mixed cluster silently mis-authorized, and R720-F1 was correctly NOT bumped. This change adds enum VARIANTS to the replicated command type, which is a different animal: `YubabaRequest` is externally tagged with no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so an epoch-3 node receiving a replicated ClaimTenant entry over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "ClaimTenant"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance its state machine past that log index, and diverges. Verified by test rather than asserted from serde's documented behaviour: raft::tests::an_unknown_request_variant_fails_to_parse_which_is_why_r732_bumped_both_epochs, which also fails loudly if anyone later adds a catch-all variant and makes this entry untrue. The break is CONDITIONAL — a mixed cluster works normally until the first tenant claim is committed — but making that window visible to the operator is exactly what advertising the epoch on GET /health is for. Reverse direction is safe: an epoch-4 node reads every epoch-3 entry unchanged. Cheap moment taken, same reasoning as history "3": the tenants map does not exist before this change, so no fleet has a tenant ownership record and nothing is in flight during the roll.
cluster_protocol_history.5: R737-F1 (W246) — tenant PLACEMENT INTENT, separate from ownership. `YubabaRequest` gained two variants (SetTenantPlacement, ClearTenantPlacement), `YubabaState` gained `placement: BTreeMap<TenantId, TenantPlacement>` (#[serde(default)]), and `MemberInfo` + `YubabaRequest::SetMember` each gained `capacity: Option<NodeCapacity>` (#[serde(default)]). THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE SAME ONE R732-F1 RECORDED, and it is the variants alone that force this: `YubabaRequest` is externally tagged with no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so an epoch-4 node receiving a replicated SetTenantPlacement over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "SetTenantPlacement"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance past that log index, and diverges. Pinned by raft::tests::an_unknown_request_variant_fails_to_parse_which_is_why_r732_bumped_both_epochs, which covers the mechanism rather than the specific variant name. THE FIELDS DID NOT NEED IT, checked rather than assumed. `capacity` is a tolerated struct field in both directions (the R720-F1 `digest` precedent, correctly NOT bumped), and the R706 hazard — a tolerated field that makes a mixed cluster silently WRONG rather than visibly broken — does not apply here. R706 bit because an old node dropped `access` and then served the secret to anybody. An old node dropping `capacity` records None, and None is defined as capacity-UNKNOWN, which YubabaState::node_headroom refuses to schedule onto. The degradation is fail-closed: the mixed window costs placement ONTO the un-upgraded nodes, never a placement that overcommits one. Same shape as R734-F5's region residual. NOTHING READS PLACEMENT YET — the scheduler is R737-F3. This ticket lands the state model and its publisher, so the mixed window has no behaviour to be wrong about beyond the divergence the variants already force.
cluster_protocol_history.6: R118-T5 (W138) part 2 - per-node boot health as a rollout step gate. `YubabaRequest` gained `ReportNodeHealth{rollout_id,node,verdict,detail,reported_at}`, `YubabaResponse` gained `NodeHealth(NodeHealthOutcome)`, and `YubabaState` gained `rollout_health: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, NodeHealthRecord>>` (#[serde(default)]). BREAKING for exactly the reason entry "4" gives and for no new one: the new variant is on `YubabaRequest`, which is `D` in declare_raft_types and therefore what EntryPayload::Normal carries, so an epoch-5 node that receives a replicated ReportNodeHealth entry over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "ReportNodeHealth"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance its state machine past that log index, and diverges. The mechanism is already pinned by raft::tests::an_unknown_request_variant_fails_to_parse_which_is_why_r732_bumped_both_epochs. This is deliberately NOT resting on the two R118-T5 part-1 re-records above it, which were correctly not bumped: those added struct FIELDS to an existing variant, plus a variant on `YubabaResponse` (`R`, which is in neither the log nor the snapshot). Adding a variant to `D` is the case entry "4" drew the line at. The break is CONDITIONAL in the same way - a mixed cluster is fine until the first plinth files a boot-health report - and making that window visible to the operator is the point of the number.
cluster_protocol_history.7: R118-F8 (W138/W158) - the membership ratchet's evidence channel. `YubabaRequest` gained two variants (ReportPeerLiveness, RecordMembershipRatchet), `YubabaResponse` gained `PeerLiveness(PeerLivenessOutcome)`, and `YubabaState` gained `peer_liveness` + `last_membership_ratchet` (both #[serde(default)]). Decided exactly as history entry "4" (R732-F1) and "6" (R118-T5 part 2) were, on the same discriminator this file has now stated three times: added struct FIELDS are tolerated in both directions, added VARIANTS on the externally-tagged YubabaRequest are not. `YubabaRequest` has no #[serde(other)] catch-all, so an epoch-6 node receiving a replicated ReportPeerLiveness over AppendEntries gets `unknown variant "ReportPeerLiveness"`, cannot apply it, cannot advance past that log index, and diverges. NOT the R720-F1 shape (a tolerated diagnostic field) and NOT the R734-T1 shape (a new route carrying an existing payload, which degrades via the 404 rule) - this one puts new bytes into the replicated command type. The break is conditional and therefore quiet until it bites: a mixed 6/7 cluster runs normally until the first peer-liveness report is committed. Both new variants are additive and neither changes any existing variant's encoding (pinned by raft::tests::a_pre_f8_binary_still_applies_the_requests_it_understands). AMENDED 2026-09-09 by R118-F8 part 2 (rehydration), in the SAME unshipped delta and therefore with NO further bump. Three additions, none of them a new break: `PeerLivenessRecord` gained `since` (#[serde(default)], the continuously-since latch the promotion hold-down is measured against); `ClusterPolicy` gained `membership_ratchet.promote_hold_down_secs` (process config, not replicated, on no wire); and on a cluster whose ratchet is running, POST /raft/add-learner now INTERROGATES the joiner - GET {addr}/raft/status for its raft term, GET {addr}/health for its build epochs - refusing 409 for a foreign incarnation and 502 for a joiner it cannot ask. THAT LAST ONE ADDS NO REQUEST FIELD: `RaftAddLearnerRequest` is {node_id, addr} and nothing the joiner sends is read, which is what makes the check unskippable. A Frozen cluster does not dial at all. The two epochs are already breaking for the request variants, so extending the same delta changes nothing about what an operator has to notice; amended here rather than opening a fourth number for a change no build has yet seen.

state_epoch_history.1: openraft 0.9 storage-v1 on-disk raft log + snapshot layout

state_epoch_history.3: R732-F1 (W245) — tenant fencing epochs, disk side of the same change as cluster_protocol "4". NEW-READS-OLD holds: `tenants` is #[serde(default)], so an epoch-3 binary loads a pre-R732 snapshot with an empty map — which denies every write rather than assuming ownership it has no record of (pinned by raft::tests::pre_r732_snapshot_without_tenants_field_loads_owning_nothing). ROLL BACK is what breaks, and this axis explicitly claims it. The blocker is the LOG, not the snapshot: store.rs persists raft_log.json as serde_json over `BTreeMap<u64, Entry>` whose payload is the same `YubabaRequest` enum as the wire, and load reads that map whole — so a single retained (un-purged) ClaimTenant / TransferTenant / RenewTenantLease entry makes a downgraded epoch-2 binary fail to deserialize its own log at startup. It does not lose a feature; it does not start. The snapshot direction is fine both ways (YubabaState has no deny_unknown_fields, so an old binary silently drops the `tenants` key), and openraft does eventually purge applied entries — but a snapshot does not retire a log entry the moment it is applied, so there is always a window, and 'reversible only if you are lucky about purge timing' is not what this axis promises. This is the first state_epoch bump that is not an openraft storage migration; the criterion is the axis's own claim, not the shape of the precedents. Same cheap moment as the wire axis: no fleet log contains a tenant entry today, so a rollback taken before the first claim is still clean.
state_epoch_history.4: R737-F1 (W246) — same change, and it moves this axis for the LOG, not for the snapshot. The snapshot half is a non-event: `placement` on YubabaState and `capacity` on MemberInfo are both #[serde(default)], so an epoch-3 snapshot loads on the new binary declaring nothing and unschedulable, and a new snapshot loads on the old binary with the unknown fields dropped. What breaks is the ROLLBACK question this axis actually asks. `raft_log.json` is a BTreeMap<u64, Entry> of serde_json, and an Entry's payload is EntryPayload::Normal(YubabaRequest) — so a log that has ever carried a SetTenantPlacement cannot be deserialized by an epoch-3 binary at all, and the node does not start rather than starting wrong. Identical reasoning to R732-F1's entry on this axis; recorded again rather than cross-referenced because the next reader will be deciding about a different change and needs the mechanism, not a pointer.

It does not lose the feature; it does not start. The snapshot direction is fine both ways (YubabaState has no deny_unknown_fields, so an old binary silently drops the `rollout_health` key), and openraft does purge applied entries eventually - but a snapshot does not retire a log entry the moment it is applied, so there is always a window.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING on either axis — both surfaces re-recorded, cluster_protocol stays 5 and state_epoch stays 4. TWO sessions' work is in this diff and each verdict was made by the session that wrote its half; neither was taken on trust. cluster_protocol moved on `rust-file .../raft/mod.rs` alone (ccb1e7d0… -> 954b65f8…) and that file is entirely R859-F2's. state_epoch moved on mod.rs plus `rust-file .../raft/store.rs` (5c423d46… -> 168adad5…), and store.rs carries exactly two contributors' hunks — R859-F2's two read accessors and R869's `applied_state()` + `seed_state_machine()`. Checked by `git diff -U0` on both files before writing, so no third party's unanalysed change was swept into this verdict.
surface_rerecords.cause: R859-F2 phase A — ship each machine's public-ingress declaration to the nodes, so the raft leader can act on an `ingress_owner` change or a node death. A fleet node never loads `.yah/infra/machines/`, so before this the leader could observe both and resolve neither to a provider, a floating IP or a public address. `MemberInfo` and `YubabaRequest::SetMember` each gained `provider`, `location`, `ingress_floating_ip` and `public_address`. Landing alongside: R869's off-fleet raft-state backup, which added two non-test items to store.rs, a new `state_backup` module and a `yubaba state` subcommand — and no replicated type.
why_not_a_bump: R859-F2 HALF (cluster_protocol + its share of state_epoch): four `Option<String>` fields with `#[serde(default)]`, added to one struct and one enum variant — byte-identical in shape to `machine`, which surface_rerecords[2026-09-05] already ruled NOT BREAKING on the SAME struct and the SAME variant. Old-reads-new silently drops the unknown keys (there is no `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` anywhere in the YubabaRequest/MemberInfo chain, and every raft RPC and both on-disk files are self-describing JSON); new-reads-old defaults them to None. openraft applies identical log bytes on every node, so there is no state-machine divergence path either. Pinned by the existing a_pre_r859_f2_snapshot_loads_untagged_and_a_downgrade_reads_a_tagged_one and a_pre_r859_f2_set_member_still_applies_with_no_machine, which cover exactly this shape.

NONE OF THE NEW FIELDS IS LOAD-BEARING FOR CONSENSUS. They are annotation on a member row, read only by the ingress effector (yubaba::ingress_effector, leader-only, opt-in behind YUBABA_INGRESS_APEX). A node running the old binary in a mixed cluster publishes a row without them, which reads as *undeclared* and makes that machine un-actable — degrading toward the pre-R859-F2 behaviour (the effector does nothing) and never below it. Same degradation shape R734-F5's region residual and R737-F1's capacity residual already have.

R869 HALF (state_epoch), verdict by @Ashguard:dove, quoted verbatim: "state_epoch, R869 half: NOT BREAKING. raft/store.rs gained two non-test items — `YubabaStateMachine::applied_state()` (a read accessor returning the applied state and its index under one lock) and a free `seed_state_machine(dir, &state)` that writes a `raft_state.json` in the format `open()` already reads, refusing any dir that holds one of the four raft files. Plus three `#[cfg(test)]` tests. No serialised type moved, no field added or removed, no file renamed, no on-disk layout change. Old-reads-new and new-reads-old are the identical shape; `seed_state_machine` writes `{last_applied: null, last_membership: <default>, state}`, which is a `StateMachineData` any build in this epoch already deserialises."

R859-F2's OWN store.rs HUNKS ARE THE SAME KIND: `floating_ip_machines()` and `public_address_for_machine()` are read accessors over the existing `members` map. They add no field and touch no serialised type — they exist precisely so the ingress effector reads the member map rather than inventing a second one.

THE ROLL IS SAFE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THAT IS THE POINT OF NOT BUMPING. A node rolled forward reads an old snapshot and lands `None` on all four fields; a node rolled back reads a tagged snapshot and drops the four keys it does not know. Neither can fail to start, and neither loses the fields that predate this change.

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING on either axis — both surfaces re-recorded, cluster_protocol stays 5 and state_epoch stays 4. One input moved on each axis and it is the same file: `rust-file oss/yubaba/crates/yubaba/src/raft/mod.rs` (2ac4dd02… -> a593344e…). The verdict is unusually cheap to make because the diff has exactly two hunks and NEITHER is a production item: one comment block inside `apply`'s ClaimTenant arm, and two new `#[test]` functions inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. `git diff -U0` on the file shows `@@ -1375,0 +1376,9 @@` (all `//` lines) and `@@ -1976,0 +1986,58 @@ mod tests`, nothing else. The hasher strips comments (SurfaceInput::RustFile -> strip_rust_comments) but not `#[cfg(test)]` items, which is why an epoch-neutral change still turns the gate red here.
surface_rerecords.cause: R869 — total-loss recovery for the raft state. The session established the recovery semantics and landed the evidence for them; it deliberately landed NO change to the replicated types. What is new in yubaba is two unit tests pinning the arithmetic the recovery runbook depends on (`repeated_self_reclaims_lift_a_rebuilt_cluster_over_the_sinks_epoch`, `the_recovery_claim_is_the_wire_shape_already_deployed`) plus the integration proofs in tests/raft_rebuild_fencing.rs. The off-fleet read half landed in turso-backup (`stream::read_fence_state`), which is not an input to either axis.
why_not_a_bump: NO REPLICATED TYPE MOVED. YubabaRequest, YubabaResponse, YubabaState, MemberInfo and TenantOwnership are byte-identical to the previous surface; the only non-comment additions in the file are behind #[cfg(test)] and are not compiled into the binary a peer talks to or the log a rollback reads.

THE ALTERNATIVE WAS A BUMP AND WAS REJECTED FOR THAT REASON, which is the part worth carrying forward. The obvious implementation of the recovery is a `min_epoch: u64` field on ClaimTenant so a rebuilt cluster can jump its epoch over the one the R2 sink already carries. That field would be #[serde(default)] and therefore TOLERATED in both directions — which is exactly the R706 hazard, not the R720-F1/R737-F1 `capacity` precedent. A node on an older binary drops `min_epoch` and applies `current + 1` while an upgraded node applies `max(current, min_epoch) + 1`: one log entry, two applied epochs, state machines diverged. That is a bump on BOTH axes (cluster_protocol 5->6 for the wire, state_epoch 4->5 because raft_log.json replays the same enum).

AND A BUMP WOULD HAVE MADE THE RECOVERY WORSE, not just more expensive. A disaster-recovery mechanism gated on a fleet-wide binary upgrade cannot be used in the disaster it exists for. The shipped recovery instead lifts the epoch with repeated plain `ClaimTenant` writes over the generic POST /raft/write that R732-T4 already deployed (raft/mod.rs:98) — one committed entry per epoch of the gap, on a path that runs once per disaster, and usable against the binaries on the fleet today.
residual_risk: THE CORRECTNESS HALF OF R869 IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS CHANGE AND NO EPOCH HIDES THAT. The epoch floor lets a rebuilt cluster write again; it does NOT fence a node resurrected from the dead fleet, because the sidecar's epoch is the highest anyone WROTE under, not the highest the dead raft group GRANTED. Proven, not argued: raft_rebuild_fencing::an_epoch_floor_alone_loses_to_a_survivor_that_outranks_it. Closing it needs the off-fleet pointer generation to reach the streamer, which is R736-F6's ratified design call (streamer.rs:144/:441 still pass 0).

surface_rerecords.verdict: NOT BREAKING — state_epoch_surface re-recorded (7811ac8f… -> 1b7e11f3…), the epoch stays 4. This closes R836-B2, which the 2026-09-01 entry below left open on the belief that no verdict had ever been made for this change. That belief was wrong and the correction is the main thing to carry forward: the verdict WAS made, by R841-B1's own author, and it is annotated in the file the drift is about — oss/yubaba/crates/yubaba/src/raft/store.rs, the `EPOCH VERDICT` @yah:gotcha in its module doc, recording the re-record 5d01cc38… -> 7811ac8f…. What went stale was the INPUT digest, not the verdict: store.rs was edited again inside the same ticket after that --write (the 'wiped raft dir' case, R841-B1's DISCOVERED WORK 3) and only then committed, as bb33160b. So 35915ec3… was a mid-ticket snapshot of a change whose analysis already existed, and the 2026-09-01 pass restored it by hand believing it was the pre-change value.
surface_rerecords.cause: R841-B1 (committed in bb33160b, 'mesofact dist') — the raft store now persists `last_purged_log_id` and the `committed` watermark to a NEW file, raft_meta.json, and writes raft_log.json / raft_vote.json / raft_meta.json through tmp+rename+fsync instead of a bare write. Before it, `last_purged_log_id` was in-memory only, so a voter that had purged its log reported `None` on every cold start and openraft exited 1 reading LogIndex(0).
why_not_a_bump: NEW-READS-OLD IS THE FIX, not a hazard. An old raft dir has no raft_meta.json, so LogMeta::default() loads and `reconstruct_last_purged` derives the marker from raft_state.json — exactly, not by guessing: purging leaves no hole, so the purge point is first_index-1, and everything at or below it is applied hence committed hence cluster-canonical. The one refusal is a dir whose log was purged past `last_applied`, which is a replica no build could rebuild from its own files, and it fails with a message naming the recovery.

OLD-READS-NEW IS A NO-OP. A pre-R841 binary opens raft_log.json / raft_state.json / raft_vote.json by exact name and has no knowledge of raft_meta.json. None of those three schemas changed, and the atomic-write change alters only HOW the same bytes land. Rollback loses the purge-marker fix — i.e. it is as broken as it always was — but reads everything it wrote.

NOTHING REPLICATED MOVED. LogMeta is node-local recovery state, never a raft request field, never in a snapshot or a log entry, so no peer parses it. That is the same reasoning the 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-01 entries used on the other axis, applied to the axis this change actually touches.

A BUMP WOULD ASSERT SOMETHING FALSE. state_epoch = 5 claims an epoch-4 dir is unreadable by this binary. It is readable — a migration exists and is tested. Recording that claim to be safe is the failure mode the history itself is vulnerable to: the epochs are only worth what their entries mean, and one bumped for an additive file with an exact migration devalues every real bump next to it.
residual_risk: ROLL FORWARD -> BACK -> FORWARD ACROSS A PURGE is the one shape this change does not handle, and it is a code gap rather than an epoch question. `open()` reconstructs the marker only when it is absent (store.rs, `if meta.last_purged_log_id.is_none()`) and drops it only when the log and the state machine are both gone; a marker that is PRESENT is trusted without being checked against the log's actual first index. So: new binary writes raft_meta.json, operator rolls back, the old binary purges further and cannot update a file it does not know about, roll forward — and the new binary reports a purge point below where the log now starts. openraft then reads an entry that was deleted and the node fails to start with the same `log entry not found` this ticket fixed. It fails loudly, on startup, with no divergence and no wrong answer served, which is why it is residual risk and not a bump: an epoch cannot fix it, and validating the marker against `entries.first()` on open can. Filed as a child of R836-B2.

The verdict was made by reading the current store.rs, not by diffing against the 35915ec3… snapshot — that tree was never committed and no longer exists. That is the right basis anyway (the question is whether the code on disk breaks mixed operation), but it means the specific late edits are attested by R841-B1's own handoffs rather than reconstructed.

One input moved and only one: `rust-items lib.rs fn raft_*` (06b66ba6… -> 9bb7aa88…), because raft_status and raft_add_learner each grew JSON keys. The route-table slice (`rust-lines lib.rs containing /raft/`) is byte-identical — R736-T3 adds no route — and raft/mod.rs, raft/network.rs and the openraft pin are all untouched, so no peer sends or parses anything new. surface_rerecords.cause: R736-T3 (W250) — cell tagging. `yubaba serve --jurisdiction <label>` makes a node's sovereign group a residency CELL; GET /raft/status gains `jurisdiction` (always emitted, null when undeclared) and an optional `cell` section {id, jurisdiction, regions}; POST /raft/add-learner gains a second gate (cell::judge) refusing a joiner in a different jurisdiction, and reports `cell_judged` / `jurisdiction` in its 200 body. The cell id IS the sovereign-group label, so no new identity is introduced anywhere on the wire.
why_not_a_bump: NEW-DIALS-OLD degrades exactly as designed and is INERT today. The only cross-node read here is the leader's operator-path GET of a joiner's /raft/status (sovereign_group::ask_peer, not a raft RPC). An old build omits the `jurisdiction` key entirely, which resolves to PeerJurisdiction::Unsupported and refuses the join — but ONLY when the target cluster itself declares a jurisdiction, which requires a flag that does not exist on any deployed build. surface_rerecords.cause: R118-T5, second pass: the lost-update race between a rollout's two legitimate writers. The engine and an operator override both read-modify-write the whole record and both move `status`, so an override landing between the engine's read and its next step advance was silently reverted - the same bug the pass had just fixed, reintroduced under concurrency and defeatable by a rollout's own step cadence. That is the fail-safe direction and was chosen over a required field for it: an entry or a hand-rolled POST /raft/write that omits the field can only create a record that does not exist, never overwrite a live one. The cost is that such a write fails silently-ish (Stale, logged) rather than failing to parse; the benefit is that the guard cannot be bypassed by forgetting it. Note also that ClearRolloutState is guarded uniformly rather than after an argument about whether it can race - a delete that expects revision 0 matches no live record and so deletes nothing.
